thought.text: Found it — my `echo` added a trailing newline to `.home`, so `isDirectorySync("/opt/android-studio\n")` fails. Rewriting without newline:

reasoning_content:
Still unknown. Why? fromHomeDot reads the `.home` file (version 2026.2.1.8, major>=4.1, Linux → dotHomeFilePath = homeDotDir/.home = /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/.home ✓ exists, installPath=/opt/android-studio ✓ directory exists → returns AndroidStudio(installPath, version: 2026.2.1.8).

But wait — maybe it's being found via a "well-known path" check (checkWellKnownPath /opt/android-studio) with version null, and `alreadyFoundStudioAt(path)` — the studios list... Order: first the home dot scan adds the studio with version. Then the well-known path check: `if (globals.fs.isDirectorySync(path) && !alreadyFoundStudioAt(path))` — alreadyFoundStudioAt(path) with no newerThan → checks whether any studio.directory == path → true (our versioned one) → skipped. So the versioned one should remain.

Hmm, but the output still says unknown. Did the home dot scan even run? directoriesToSearch = [homeDir, .cache/Google if exists] — .cache/Google exists ✓. listSync(followLinks: false).whereType<Directory>() → AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8 ✓ matches regex `^\.?(AndroidStudio[^\d]*)([\d.]+)` — group1=AndroidStudio, group2=2026.2.1.8 ✓.

fromHomeDot: versionMatch.groupCount — wait, the matcher is `^\.?(AndroidStudio[^\d]*)([\d.]+)` — it has 2 groups so groupCount==2 ✓ (groupCount is the number of groups = 2, and the check is `?.groupCount != 2` → pass).

Version.parse("2026.2.1.8") → versionPattern `^(\d+)(\.(\d+)(\.(\d+))?)?` → major=2026 minor=2 patch=1 ✓ non-null.

major=2026 >=4, minor=2 >=1 → dotHomeFilePath = homeDotDir.path/.home → /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/.home ✓ → read → "/opt/android-studio\n" → isDirectorySync ✓ → AndroidStudio(installPath, version 2026.2.1.8).

So it should be versioned... Unless the well-known path scan runs first and a version-null entry for /opt/android-studio gets added, and then our home dot entry is skipped by alreadyFoundStudioAt! Order in _allLinuxOrWindows: 1) home dot scan (adds versioned entry), 2) Windows, 3) configured, 4) Linux well-known path. So the home dot entry is added first...

But wait, the home dot scan might have failed because the regex `[\d.]+` is... "2026.2.1.8" — no problem.

Hmm, or maybe flutter doctor is caching? Does the Flutter tool cache the Android Studio detection? No, it's per-invocation.

Wait — maybe the issue is: `listSync(followLinks: false)` against the homeDir — does it include hidden directories? listSync by default does not list hidden files! The default for FileSystemEntity.list is `followLinks: true`, and hidden files are skipped by default (Linux: names starting with '.' are excluded unless includeHidden... actually, does Dart's ListSync have an `includeHidden`? Hmm, in the Dart VM on Linux, does Directory.listSync include dotfiles by default? Let me think... dart:io Directory.list: "If followLinks is false... Hidden files and directories are included" — actually I don't remember. In dart:io, does list() include hidden files by default? The docs say "The file system is responsible for... hidden files" — I think Dart's Directory.list includes hidden files by default (unlike glob). Hmm.

But wait — the earlier detection (version unknown) already proves that .cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8 was found via home dot (it's the only path that produces /opt/android-studio with that directory name... no wait — the well-known path check also adds /opt/android-studio with version null! checkWellKnownPath("/opt/android-studio")? Let me look at what well-known paths are checked on Linux. Let me look at lines 467–490.

If the well-known path check adds /opt/android-studio with version null, and the home dot entry didn't get added (because hidden directories were skipped), then result = unknown version — which matches the observation!

Let me verify: is .cache/Google listed? listSync on $HOME by default — does it include hidden directories? The Dart VM on Linux: I think Directory.list includes hidden files by default (no filter). Hmm, then the home dot should be found.

Or maybe the .home file read is: readAsStringSync on "/opt/android-studio\n" — installPath="/opt/android-studio\n" → isDirectorySync with trailing newline → fails! isDirectorySync("/opt/android-studio\n") → false → returns null!! That's it! When I wrote the file with echo, I appended a trailing newline! The first time I wrote it with echo (with newline) to the wrong location; now I also used echo → again a trailing newline.

Fix: printf '%s' without a newline.

action.command: printf '%s' "/opt/android-studio" > /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/.home && od -c /root/.cache/Google/AndroidStudio2026.2.1.8/.home | tail -2 && export ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk && cd /workspace && fvm flutter doctor -v 2>&1 | grep -v "Woah\|superuser"; echo "exit: ${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
